extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level, multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks. It contains 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated in three stages: selecting subjects based on common university majors and the presence of visual inputs, ruling out subjects with insufficient multimodal problems, and recruiting contributors to collect questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across 30 subjects in six disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected/created by recruited university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant majors, following instructions on copyright/licensing and avoiding questions with immediately available answers; quality control included duplicate detection and author review, format/typo checking, and author-assigned difficulty labeling with very easy items removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control involved duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review of suspected duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and difficulty categorization with exclusion of about 10% very easy problems.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college/university students, including co-authors, specializing in various disciplines/majors; elsewhere the paper also describes 50 college students from various disciplines and subjects.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used as automated tools to identify potential duplicate problems during quality control.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases introduced by manual curation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has limitations: manual curation may introduce bias, and its focus on college-level subjects may be insufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating large multimodal models on expert-level capabilities, including basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning across professional domains.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Subjects were filtered/selected for inclusion based on whether visual inputs are commonly adopted and whether enough relevant multimodal problems could be found; subjects like law and linguistics were ruled out, resulting in 30 selected subjects from six disciplines.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models

description.evidence: We introduce MMMU: a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “Our benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, we go through the common university majors to decide what subjects should be included in our benchmark... Through this principle, we rule out a few subjects like law and linguistics because it is difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems in these subjects.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations... the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers... Data Quality Control... lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems... reviewed by the authors... distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors... The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy... are excluded from the benchmark.”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects” and “we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The introduction of MMMU marks a significant step towards evaluating the capabilities of LMMs in the context of Expert AGI. By assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains, MMMU provides a comprehensive benchmark

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The selection is based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in the subjects to provide valuable information. Through this principle, we rule out a few subjects like law and linguistics because it is difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems in these subjects. Consequently, we select 30 subjects from six different disciplines.
